newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-RONALDO FREE KICK GIVES BRAZIL WIN OVER BOSNIA.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-RONALDO FREE KICK GIVES BRAZIL WIN OVER BOSNIA.

text.p: Striker Ronaldo scored from a controversially awarded free kick to give world champions Brazil a 1-0 win at home to Bosnia in a drab friendly international on Wednesday.
Ronaldo blasted a low, powerful shot through a poorly-organised Bosnian defensive wall from 20 metres in the 67th minute just as the 20,000 crowd were beginning to get on their team.
The free kick was awarded for a foul on Brazil playmaker Djalminha, who did not appear to be touched by a Bosnian player as he fell to the ground in melodramatic style.
Fourteen of the 22-strong Brazilian squad had been on holiday for two weeks before the match and the lethargy with which most of the team played suggested they had just been dragged off a beach.
Although the final of the Brazilian championship was played Sunday, 16 of the 24 clubs had been eliminated a fortnight earlier.
Bosnia, most of whose players had come from sub-zero temperatures in Europe, defended stubbornly but wilted in the dripping humidity of Manaus, which lies in the heart of the Amazon rain forest.
Brazil coach Mario Zagallo criticised his squad's opponents. "I was told their coach promised they would attack but they never tried to come out, they just stayed at the back," he complained.
Ronaldo, who recently had his salary with Spanish club Barcelona doubled to a reported $3.85 million a year, has not scored for more than a month in Spain and struggled to escape the Bosnian marking.
On the one occasion he got away, he wasted an excellent chance by firing over the crossbar from close range after Cafu had pulled the ball back to him in the 53rd minute.

Palmeiras midfielder Djalminha also showed little inspiration, Ronaldo's Barcelona teammate Giovanni barely touched the ball and it was left to 19-year-old Denilson to show some spark in the Brazilian midfield.
The home crowd were begining to jeer just before the goal. But Brazil perked up late in the game, forcing several high-quality saves from Mirsad Dedic.

Bosnia, who surprisingly beat Italy 2-1 at home in a friendly last month, were limited in attack but nearly scored in the second minute when striker Elvir Bolic had a free kick turned around the post by Zetti.
Bosnia's star striker also hit the post in the 30th minute after the ball was farcially passed to him by Brazil defender Andre Cruz in the Brazil penalty area.

Bosnia, who earlier this month were given permission by soccer's governing body FIFA to play their home World Cup qualifying matches in the capital city Sarajevo, had four players booked in a rough first half.
Brazil, who qualify automatically for the 1998 World Cup in France, have played 10 full internationals this year, losing once against Mexico in January.

Brazil - 1-Zetti, 2-Cafu, 3-Goncalves, 4-Andre Cruz, 6-Ze Roberto (16-Junior, 73rd minute), 5-Leandro, 8-Flavio Conceicao (18-Ricardinho, 46th), 10-Djalminha (19-Rodrigo, 73rd), 11- Denilson, 7-Giovanni (7-Oseas, 77th), 9-Ronaldo

Bosnia - 1-Mirsad Dedic, 2-Sead Kapetanovic, 5-Nudzein Geca, 3-Bakir Besirevic, 4-Samin Pintul 6-Ramcic, 7-Vlatko Glavas (13- Dadic, 77th), 8-Senad Bejic (14-Turkovic, 62nd), 11-Nermin Sabic (15-Vedin Music, 62nd), 9-Elvir Bolic, 10-Hasan Salihamidzic (16-Osmic, 86th).
